summary: This page from the Delhi EE&REM Centre describes solar thermal applications, covering low-temperature systems for heating water and air and high-temperature concentrating systems for steam and power. It explains flat plate and evacuated tube solar water heaters, gives hot water requirement rules of thumb, and lists Delhi's mandatory solar water heating building categories and subsidy schemes for non-commercial and domestic sectors. It also notes central government cost support for concentrating solar systems used in community kitchens and steam applications.
one_line: Delhi government page explaining solar thermal applications, solar water heater types, mandatory use rules, and subsidies.
key_facts: Solar thermal systems can collect the sun's energy to create high temperature steam (greater than 100oC) and low temperature heat (less than 100oC).
A solar water heater's recirculated water through the absorber panel raises the temperature to 80oC (maximum) on a good sunny day.
Flat Plate Collectors use an insulated outer metallic box covered with glass sheet and selectively coated blackened metallic absorber sheets.
There are 83 BIS approved manufacturers of Solar Flat Plate Collectors, according to the note.
Evacuated Tube Collectors are made of double layer borosilicate glass tubes evacuated for insulation.
There are 14 MNES approved ETC based solar water heating suppliers, and buyers should check test reports issued by the Ministry of Non-conventional Energy Sources, Govt. of India.

Vide Delhi Government Gazette Notification No. F.11 (149)/2004-Power/2387 dated 28/09/2006, solar water heating is mandatory for listed building categories including hospitals, hotels, and large canteens serving more than one hundred persons a day.

Residential buildings on plots of 500 square meters or above in the National Capital Territory of Delhi must use solar water heating, excluding Delhi Cantonment Area or areas exempted under section 61 of the Energy Conservation Act, 2001.
Under Cabinet decision no.1309 dated 20.11.07, non-commercial institutions receive Rs.6000 per 100 lpd SWHS, up to a maximum of Rs. 60,000 for a 1000 lpd system.
The domestic sector subsidy gives a fixed incentive/rebate of Rs.6000 on installation of a Solar Water Heating System.
Parabolic dish systems concentrate solar radiation to a single point to produce temperatures in excess of 1000oC.
Line-focus parabolic concentrators generate temperatures of about 350oC along a single axis.
Under the Scheffler dish programme, MNES provides 50% of system cost up to Rs.5,000 per sq. mtr. of dish area for non-profit institutions.
For commercial and industrial organizations, MNES provides 35% of system cost up to Rs.3500 per sq. mtr. of dish area.
